Ramses

precepts.text: They departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month, on the morrow after the passover.
precepts.point: The children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, beside children. Israel departed from Rameses in the first month; the exodus is tied to Rameses by name.
precepts.why:
“And the children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, beside children.” The exodus is tied to Rameses by name, and Numbers dates it: “they departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the morrow after the passover the children of Israel went out with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians.”

Israel departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day, the morrow after the passover, with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians. Six hundred thousand men on foot beside children, leaving Rameses openly the morrow after the passover: the same departure, the same place, the same month.

precepts.text: These are the journeys of Israel by their armies, and Moses wrote their goings out by the commandment of the Lord, departing from Rameses on the morrow after the Passover.
precepts.point: Moses wrote their goings out by the commandment of the Lord. The Lord gave the word, and great was the company of those that published it; so the claim that another people wrote the scriptures falls, for Moses wrote what God commanded him to write.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

precepts.why:
Numbers 33 is the record of the journeys that bring Israel to the wilderness of Sinai in the third month: “These are the journeys of the children of Israel, which went forth out of the land of Egypt with their armies under the hand of Moses and Aaron.” Israel went forth out of Egypt with their armies.

“And Moses wrote their goings out according to their journeys by the commandment of the Lord”. Moses wrote, and he wrote by the commandment of the Lord. So the claim that another people wrote the scriptures falls; Moses wrote what God commanded him to write.

The journey begins on a set day: “And they departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the morrow after the passover the children of Israel went out with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians. For the Egyptians buried all their firstborn, which the Lord had smitten among them: upon their gods also the Lord executed judgments.” From that day in the first month, the journeys run to the third month, when Israel camped before the mount.

precepts.text: They departed from Rephidim and pitched in the wilderness of Sinai, the same arrival Exodus 19 records in the third month.
precepts.point: Moses wrote their goings out by the commandment of the Lord. The Lord gave the word, and great was the company of those that published it; so the claim that another people wrote the scriptures falls, for Moses wrote what God commanded him to write.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

precepts.why:
“And they departed from Rephidim, and pitched in the wilderness of Sinai.” This is the same arrival Exodus 19 records: “they were departed from Rephidim, and were come to the desert of Sinai, and had pitched in the wilderness”.

Numbers 33 gives the journey, from Rameses on the morrow after the Passover to Rephidim to the wilderness of Sinai, and Exodus 19 gives the time: the third month after going forth out of Egypt. The two records line up.

precepts.text: The nations left remaining become snares and traps, scourges in your sides and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off the good land.
precepts.point: They are going to be problems, because they are not following the Most High as Israel follows; if you allow them to stay in your land they will always cause problems.

note.label: Numbers 33: The Journeys of Israel from Egypt to the Plains of Moab

precepts.why:
“But if ye will not drive out the inhabitants of the land from before you; then it shall come to pass, that those which ye let remain of them shall be pricks in your eyes, and thorns in your sides, and shall vex you in the land wherein ye dwell.” Joshua repeats the warning at the end of his days: “Know for a certainty that the Lord your God will no more drive out any of these nations from before you; but they shall be snares and traps unto you, and scourges in your sides, and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off this good land which the Lord your God hath given you.”

The nations left remaining are going to be problems, because they are not following the Most High as Israel follows. If you allow them to stay in your land they will always cause problems: snares, traps, scourges and thorns, until Israel perishes from off the good land.

precepts.text: They departed from Rameses with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians; this proves which Pharaoh Israel came out from under.
precepts.point: He kept the oath sworn unto the fathers and redeemed Israel out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt; Israel came out from under Rameses.

note.label: Deuteronomy 7: A Holy People, Chosen Above All People

precepts.why:
“And they departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the morrow after the passover the children of Israel went out with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians.” This proves which Pharaoh Israel came out from under: Israel came out from under Rameses.

That is the redemption Moses speaks of, “redeemed you out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.” Not because Israel was many, “for ye were the fewest of all people”, only threescore and ten souls out of the loins of Jacob when Israel first went down, but because the Lord loved them and kept the oath sworn unto the fathers. He needs no other reason, and we should never apologize for that.

precepts.text: Ye shall divide the land by lot for an inheritance among your families; the command was given long before.
precepts.point: The land is to be divided only unto the Israelites: unto the nine tribes and the half tribe of Manasseh, for the other two and a half tribes had already received theirs. It had already been told that these lands must be divided among our people.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

precepts.why:
Long before Joshua ever stood over this land, the command was already given: “And ye shall divide the land by lot for an inheritance among your families: and to the more ye shall give the more inheritance, and to the fewer ye shall give the less inheritance: every man’s inheritance shall be in the place where his lot falleth; according to the tribes of your fathers ye shall inherit.”

That is why the Most High tells Joshua, “only divide thou it by lot unto the Israelites for an inheritance, as I have commanded thee.” The driving out of the inhabitants of the hill country of Lebanon and all the Sidonians is the Most High's own work; Joshua's part is only to divide it by lot, the way it was commanded back in Numbers. It had already been told that these lands must be divided among our people, and among no one else.

points: Follow these journeys with the maps in the back of the Bible; most Bibles have them. Seeing the wilderness of Sin, the Red sea, and the route they were taking gives a better understanding of the lands and cities being read.

The number is the fortieth year; read it carefully.
